details: The European Union has unveiled its 21st sanctions package against Russia, specifically targeting crypto networks and foreign crypto platforms accused of aiding Russia in evading financial restrictions. The new measures propose to extend transaction bans to approximately 20 non-EU entities, including banks and crypto platforms. Notably, the EU may also introduce a country-level ban on crypto services from non-EU nations that host platforms facilitating sanctions evasion. This escalation aims to close loopholes used by Moscow, with stablecoins linked to Russia, such as A7A5, identified as particularly vulnerable.
title: EU Targets Crypto in New Sanctions Against Russia

details: Leading financial institutions, including JPMorgan, Citi, and Bank of America, are reportedly developing a new tokenized payment network. This initiative is seen as a strategic move to establish bank control over the tokenized settlement layer, potentially challenging the role of existing stablecoins and government-issued central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) in institutional payments. The development reflects a broader trend of traditional finance engaging with tokenization, aiming to maintain gatekeeper status in a blockchain-native financial system.
title: Major Banks Develop Tokenized Payment Network, Challenging Stablecoins
